texts.li: [theirLowtech] {DEAD}, {TITLE} of {FACTION} for as long as most can remember, died in {PLACE} three nights ago. The drums have not stopped since.\n\nThe new {TITLE} is {X_nameFull}. The colony has never met {X_objective}, but the traders have, and every one of them has an opinion.

[theirHightech] The notice from {PLACE} is brief and formal: {FACTION} announce with sorrow the death of their {TITLE}, {DEAD}, after a long illness, and the succession of {X_nameFull}.\n\nThe flags in {PLACE} are at half-mast. What the change means for the colony depends on what kind of {TITLE} {X_nameDef} turns out to be.

[winter] {DEAD}, {TITLE} of {FACTION}, did not see the end of the winter. {PLACE} buried {OTHER_objective} under a gray sky, with the whole of {FACTION} standing in the snow.\n\n{X_nameFull} leads them now.

summaries.li: [kind] {FACTION} warm to the colony, and their caravans come more often. A gift for the funeral would be noticed.
[greedy] Trade with {FACTION} picks up, at a price. A gift for the funeral would be noticed, and weighed.
[harsh] {FACTION} cool toward the colony under their new {TITLE}. A gift for the funeral might soften {X_objective}.
[steady] Little changes with {FACTION} for now. A gift for the funeral would be noticed.

texts.li: {FACTION} will bury {DEAD} in {PLACE} in a few days, and the neighbors are expected to send something, even if it's only a few words.\n\nThe new {TITLE} will be watching who does.

[greedy] {FACTION} will bury {DEAD} in {PLACE} in a few days. Neighbors are expected to send something.\n\nThe traders say {X_nameDef} keeps a list of who sent what. It's a long list, and it has numbers in it.

li.label: Send a gift ({COUNT} silver)
li.outcome: A rider from {PLACE} takes the gift from the gate, with a note for the new {TITLE}. It will be there in time for the funeral.

li.label: Send words of respect
li.outcome: A letter goes to {PLACE}, saying the things neighbors say at times like this.

li.label: Send nothing
li.outcome: The colony sends nothing to {PLACE}. It's noticed.

texts.li: {X_nameDef} has settled into the seat at {PLACE}, and the region is learning what that means: a short temper, a long memory, and a hard line with most of the neighbors.\n\nNot with the colony, though. {X_nameDef} remembers the gift at the funeral, and has said so.

li.chronicle: {X_nameDef}, the new {TITLE} of {FACTION}, remembers the colony's gift.

texts.li: [kind,gift] {X_nameDef} has settled into the seat at {PLACE}. The roads are open, the traders are happy, and the new {TITLE} sent the colony a letter of thanks for its gift, written by hand.
[kind,!gift] The roads out of {PLACE} are open, the traders are happy, and {FACTION} are easier neighbors under {X_nameDef} than they were.

[greedy,gift] {X_nameDef} has settled into the seat at {PLACE} and gone straight to business. {FACTION}'s caravans are out on every road, and the colony's gift has put it near the top of the list of friends worth trading with.
[greedy,!gift] {FACTION}'s caravans are out on every road now that {X_nameDef} holds the seat at {PLACE}, and they drive a hard bargain.
[harsh] {FACTION} have turned inward under {X_nameDef}. Their traders come less often, and their riders are slower to wave.
[steady] {X_nameDef} has settled into the seat at {PLACE}. Little has changed so far, which may be the point.
[kind,!sameCreed] Those who know {X_nameDef} say {X_pronoun} is fair-minded and generous, and wants the roads open.
[greedy,!sameCreed] Traders say {X_nameDef} counts everything twice and likes a deal. Trade with {FACTION} should pick up, at a price.
[harsh,!sameCreed] {X_nameDef} has a reputation for a short temper and a long memory. {FACTION} are likely to be cooler toward outsiders for a while.
[steady,!sameCreed] By all accounts, {X_nameDef} is careful and in no hurry to change anything.
[sameCreed] {X_nameDef} keeps the colony's own ideoligion, and has said so in public. That counts for something in {PLACE}.

{DEAD}, {TITLE} of {FACTION}, is dying in {PLACE} and has named no heir. Two have stepped forward. {X_nameFull} is of {DEAD}'s own blood, young, careful and well liked by the traders. {OTHER_nameFull} is a war captain who has spent ten years on {FACTION}'s borders and thinks they have been soft for too long.\n\nBoth have sent riders to the neighbors. Both want to know where the colony stands.

[theirLowtech] {DEAD}, {TITLE} of {FACTION}, has taken to bed in {PLACE} and will not get up again. The hall is already split. On one side stands {X_nameFull}, {DEAD}'s child, young and cautious and liked by the merchants. On the other stands {OTHER_nameFull}, a war captain with the border garrisons behind {OTHER_objective}.\n\nWhoever the neighbors back may tip it.

summaries.li: {FACTION} will settle it within days, one way or the other. Back the winner and they will remember it; back the loser and they will remember that too.
[backHeir] The colony has backed {X_nameDef}. {FACTION} will settle it within days.
[backCaptain] The colony has backed {OTHER_nameDef}. {FACTION} will settle it within days.

texts.li:
Two riders have come to the gate within an hour of each other, one in {X_nameDef}'s colors and one in {OTHER_nameDef}'s, and each asks the same thing.

"{X_nameDef} will keep the roads open and the prices fair," says the first. "Ask your traders."

"{OTHER_nameDef} will see that {FACTION} are never pushed around again," says the second, "and remembers friends."

li.label: Back {X_nameDef}
li.outcome: The rider in {X_nameDef}'s colors leaves with the colony's word. The other leaves without it.

li.label: Back {OTHER_nameDef}
li.outcome: The rider in {OTHER_nameDef}'s colors leaves with the colony's word. The other leaves without it.

li.label: Stay out of it
li.outcome: Both riders leave without an answer. The colony will deal with whoever wins.

texts.li: {X_nameDef} is the new {TITLE} of {FACTION}. {DEAD} died the night it was settled, and {OTHER_nameDef} rode out of {PLACE} the next morning with a few loyal captains and has not been seen since.\n\n{X_nameDef} has not forgotten that the colony spoke up early.

li.chronicle: {X_nameDef} took {FACTION}'s seat, with the colony's backing.

texts.li: {X_nameDef} won {FACTION}'s seat in the end. {DEAD} is buried and {OTHER_nameDef} has gone into exile.\n\nThe new {TITLE} is polite about the colony in public. In private, by every account, {X_nameDef} remembers which side it took.

li.chronicle: {X_nameDef} took {FACTION}'s seat, against the colony's choice.

texts.li: {DEAD} died the night it was settled, and {X_nameDef} is the new {TITLE} of {FACTION}. {OTHER_nameDef} has left {PLACE} for good, the roads are quiet, and the traders are relieved.

{OTHER_nameDef} holds {FACTION}'s seat. The garrisons marched into {PLACE} the day {DEAD} died, and {X_nameDef} left by the back gate that night.\n\n{OTHER_nameDef} promised that friends would be rewarded, and the first letter under the new seal names the colony as one.

li.chronicle: {OTHER_nameDef} took {FACTION}'s seat, with the colony's backing.

texts.li: The garrisons marched into {PLACE} the day {DEAD} died, and {OTHER_nameDef} holds {FACTION}'s seat now. {X_nameDef} is in exile.\n\nThe new {TITLE} keeps a list of the neighbors who backed the wrong side, and the colony's name is near the top.

li.chronicle: {OTHER_nameDef} took {FACTION}'s seat, against the colony's choice.

texts.li: {FACTION} will be harder neighbors under {OTHER_nameDef}, to everyone. The garrisons marched into {PLACE} the day {DEAD} died, and {X_nameDef} is in exile.
The quarrel over {FACTION}'s seat has been settled in {PLACE}, behind closed doors.

The preachers of {FACTION} and {ENEMY} have fallen out in public. It began with a sermon in {PLACE} against {ITEM}, the creed of {ENEMY}, and the answer came back within the week. Now every market between the two has a preacher on a box in it, and neither side is talking about anything else.\n\nIt is a war of words, so far. Both sides would like the colony's voice.

[ourCreed] {FACTION}'s preachers have declared that {ITEM}, the creed of {ENEMY}, is a lie, and {ENEMY} have answered in kind. It has been going on for weeks.\n\n{TALE} is the colony's own ideoligion, and the preachers of {FACTION} know it. They are expecting the colony to say so out loud.

[theirCreed] The preachers of {FACTION} have started on {ITEM}, the creed of {ENEMY}, and {ENEMY} are answering back. It has been going on for weeks.\n\n{ITEM} is the colony's own ideoligion, and {ENEMY}'s preachers have already sent to ask whether the colony means to stand up for it.

summaries.li: Preachers of both creeds will come asking for the colony's support. Taking a side wins one neighbor and cools the other; a debate could win both, or neither.

texts.li: Two preachers arrived on the same morning and have been arguing at the gate since noon. One speaks for {TALE} and {FACTION}, the other for {ITEM} and {ENEMY}. Both want the colony to say, out loud, which of them is right.\n\n{A_nameDef} thinks the colony could host a proper debate instead, with both of them and anyone who wants to listen. It could go well. It could also go very badly.

li.label: Speak for {TALE}
li.outcome: The council says it plainly at the gate: {TALE} has the right of it. One preacher goes off smiling. The other is halfway down the road before the words are finished.

li.label: Speak for {ITEM}
li.outcome: {ITEM} has the right of it, the council says, and says it where both preachers can hear. One of them thanks the colony. The other spits in the dust and leaves.

li.label: Host a debate
li.outcome: The debate runs until the lamps are lit. Neither preacher gives an inch, but both leave saying the other argued well, and that the colony kept a fair table.
li.riskOutcome: The debate goes badly. By the second hour the preachers are shouting, by the third their followers are, and both leave convinced the colony set them up.
li.deed: hosted a debate between the two creeds

li.label: Keep out of it
li.outcome: Both preachers are thanked and sent on their way. The colony keeps its own counsel.

texts.li: [sideFaction] The preachers have gone home and the markets are quiet again. {FACTION} remember that the colony stood with {TALE} when it counted. {ENEMY} remember it too.
[sideEnemy] The markets are quiet again, and the preachers have gone home. {ENEMY} remember that the colony stood with {ITEM} when it counted. {FACTION} remember it too.
[debate] The quarrel between {TALE} and {ITEM} has cooled, and some in both camps say it cooled at the colony's table.
[debateFailed] The quarrel between {TALE} and {ITEM} has burned itself out, no thanks to the colony's debate, which both sides still bring up.

[!sideFaction,!sideEnemy,!debate,!debateFailed] The last preacher has left the markets, and the quarrel between {TALE} and {ITEM} has cooled. The colony stayed out of it, which neither side much liked, and neither side much minded.

{FACTION} and {ENEMY} have been at war longer than the colony has stood. This season, for the first time anyone remembers, both sides are tired enough to talk.\n\nThey need somewhere neither of them owns, and someone both of them half trust. Riders from both have asked whether that could be the colony.

[winter] A hard season has worn {FACTION} and {ENEMY} down to the point where even old enemies start counting what the war costs. Both have sent riders to the colony, separately and a day apart, with the same question: would it host the talks?

summaries.li: If the colony hosts the talks, the two may make peace for good, and both will owe the colony for it. It costs food for the delegations and a few days of everyone's patience.
[hosting] The delegations of {FACTION} and {ENEMY} will meet at the colony within days.

texts.li: The riders of {FACTION} and {ENEMY} are waiting for an answer, at opposite ends of the colony's yard. Hosting means a table, a roof, and food for both delegations, {COUNT} portions or so, and someone to keep the peace at the table.\n\n{A_nameDef} would be the one doing that. {A_nameDef} has already started thinking about the seating.

li.label: Host the talks ({COUNT} food)
li.outcome: Both riders leave with the same answer. The food is set aside, and the delegations will come within days, two sets of people who would rather not eat at the same table.

li.label: Decline
li.outcome: The riders are told the colony would rather stay out of it. The war goes on.

texts.li: After three days of talks at the colony, with {A_nameDef} keeping order at the table, {FACTION} and {ENEMY} have agreed to end their war.\n\nThe delegations left by the same gate, side by side. Both sides know where it happened.

[theirLowtech] It took three days, two walkouts and a great deal of the colony's food, but {FACTION} and {ENEMY} have sworn peace over the colony's table, with {A_nameDef} as witness.\n\nThere is a fresh dent in the table where someone brought a fist down on the second day. The colony has decided to leave it.

li.chronicle: {FACTION} and {ENEMY} made peace at the colony.

texts.li: The talks broke down on the third day, over a strip of border the colony had never heard of. The delegations left an hour apart, by different roads.\n\nThey tried, though, and both sides thanked the colony for the chance.

li.chronicle: Peace talks between {FACTION} and {ENEMY} at the colony broke down.

texts.li: The talk of peace between {FACTION} and {ENEMY} has come to nothing. Somewhere between their lands, the war goes on.

li.chronicle: Talk of peace between {FACTION} and {ENEMY} came to nothing.

texts.li: A mercenary company, {NAME}, has come down from the hills and made camp a day's march from the colony. Their captain, {X_nameFull}, has been to every settlement in the region looking for work.\n\nThey are good, by all accounts, and expensive, and not particular about who pays.

[againstWarlord] There's a war on the wind, and {NAME} has followed it into the region. Their captain, {X_nameFull}, has heard about the warlord of {ENEMY} and what's been happening to the neighbors.\n\n{X_nameDef} thinks there's money to be made in it, and is already asking who in the region has silver.

summaries.li: {X_nameDef} will offer the company's swords for hire against {ENEMY}. It ends when they ride on, with or without the colony's silver.
[hired] {NAME} rides against {ENEMY} at {PLACE} in the colony's pay. News will come within days.

texts.li: "{COUNT} silver, paid now," {X_nameDef} said at the gate, with two sergeants standing behind. "For that, {NAME} rides on {ENEMY} at {PLACE}, and you get a share of whatever we bring back."\n\nIf the colony would rather not, a hot meal for the company would be taken kindly, and they would be on their way.

[againstWarlord] {X_nameDef} came to the gate in person. For {COUNT} silver, paid now, {NAME} will ride against {ENEMY} at {PLACE}, where the warlord's band comes and goes, and the colony will get a share of whatever they bring back.\n\n{X_nameDef} doesn't promise the warlord's head. {X_nameDef} doesn't rule it out either.

li.label: Hire them ({COUNT} silver)
li.outcome: The silver changes hands, and {NAME} breaks camp the same afternoon. {X_nameDef} says to expect news within the week.

li.label: Feed the company (30 food)
li.outcome: The company's cook comes for the food with a handcart, and in the morning the company moves on, looking for work elsewhere.

li.label: Send them on
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} shrugs and goes back to camp. There are other settlements with silver.

texts.li: [!warlordFell] {NAME} came back from {PLACE} in better spirits than it left, with carts behind it. {X_nameDef} has left the colony's share at the gate and ridden on, looking for the next job.

[warlordFell] {NAME} came back from {PLACE} with carts behind it and news ahead of it: the warlord was there when the company struck, and did not get away. {X_nameDef} has left the colony's share at the gate and ridden on.

li.chronicle: {NAME}, in the colony's pay, came back from {PLACE} with spoils.

texts.li: {NAME} did not come back from {PLACE}. A few stragglers passed the colony days later, carrying their wounded, and didn't stop.\n\nThe colony's silver is gone with the rest.

li.chronicle: {NAME}, in the colony's pay, was broken at {PLACE}.

texts.li: [fed] {NAME} has moved on out of the region. {X_nameDef} sent word back with a trader: if the colony ever needs swords, it knows where to ask.
[!fed] {NAME} broke camp this morning and rode on, out of the region.

li.chronicle: {NAME} moved on out of the region.

texts.li: The road between the colony and {PLACE} has turned bad. Bandits of {ENEMY} have been stopping carts in the cuttings and taking everything, and twice now they've taken the drivers too.\n\n{FACTION}'s caravans have stopped using it. So has anyone else with sense.

[enemyHightech] Raiders of {ENEMY} have set up on the road to {PLACE} with a roadblock and a machine gun nest, and are charging a toll of everything a traveler owns. {FACTION}'s trucks have stopped running.\n\nAnyone who can find another way is taking it.

summaries.li: Caravans and visitors come less often, merchants get stranded, and the bandits may try the colony itself. Clearing the road would take silver, or patience.
[paid] Guards paid for by the colony and {FACTION} are clearing the road to {PLACE}.

titles.li: {FACTION} ask for help with the road

texts.li: A rider from {PLACE} brings word that {FACTION} mean to clear the road, and would welcome the colony's help paying for it. Guards cost money, and {COUNT} silver from the colony would get them out this week instead of next season.\n\nThe rider can take the silver back today.

li.label: Pay for guards ({COUNT} silver)
li.outcome: The rider takes the silver back to {PLACE} the long way around, well clear of the road. The guards will be out within days.
li.deed: paid for guards on the road to {PLACE}

li.label: Wish them luck
li.outcome: The rider is told the colony can't spare the silver.

li.label: Bandits from the road
li.text: The bandits on the road to {PLACE} have had a thin week, and have come to see what the colony keeps behind its walls.

texts.li: A merchant of {FACTION} walked into the colony this morning in a shirt and one boot. The bandits on the road took the rest, including the cart and the mule.\n\nThe merchant asks for a meal and a bed for the night, and promises not to forget it.

[theirHightech] A trader of {FACTION} walked in from the road this morning with nothing but the clothes on their back. The bandits took the truck, the cargo and the boots.\n\nThe trader asks for a meal and a bed for the night, and promises not to forget it.

li.label: A meal and a bed
li.outcome: The merchant eats every crumb, sleeps in the corner he's shown inside, and leaves in the morning promising to pay the colony back.

li.label: Send them on
li.outcome: The merchant is given directions to {PLACE} and walks on.

texts.li: The guards the colony helped pay for cleared the road to {PLACE} within a few days. The bandits of {ENEMY} have gone back where they came from, and the first carts are already through.\n\n{FACTION} know who paid for it.

li.chronicle: The road to {PLACE} was cleared, with the colony's silver.

texts.li: {FACTION} cleared the road to {PLACE} at last, without the colony's help. The bandits of {ENEMY} have scattered, and the carts are running again.
Whoever was robbing carts on the road to {PLACE} has moved on, to another road or another region. They weren't chased off. They ran out of carts to rob.\n\nThe traders are coming back, slowly.

li.chronicle: The bandits on the road to {PLACE} moved on.
